## Workflow conventions

- Branch per Linear issue: `feature/<sma-####>-<kebab-title>`. The branch name is pre-computed in each Linear ticket's `gitBranchName` field.
- Design artifacts per ticket (`docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`, `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>.md`) land on the feature branch alongside the implementation — not pre-merged to `main`.
- **Keep the public mdBook (`docs/book/`) current — update it in the same PR as any user-facing change.** Before opening a PR, check whether the work changes public API, the quickstart/example flow, the crate roster (incl. a stub crate ascending to published), or a documented concept; if so, bring the affected `docs/book/src/*.md` page(s) into line on the same branch. The book is published from `main` and drifts silently otherwise — it sat as the untouched SMA-311 scaffold (13/17 pages still `> **Stub.**`) through all of Stage 1 before anyone noticed; SMA-423 is the one-time catch-up, and this rule keeps the backlog from rebuilding. A pure-internal change (refactor, CI, deps, release plumbing) needs no book edit — but make that a conscious call, not a silent skip. `mdbook build docs/book` must stay clean (`[output.linkcheck] warning-policy = "error"`).
- **Keep crate `README.md` files current — update the affected crate's README in the same PR as any change to its public surface.** Each of the ten published crates' `README.md` is its crates.io (and docs.rs landing-sidebar) page — no crate sets an explicit `readme`, so Cargo uses the default `README.md`. Before opening a PR, for every crate the work touches check whether the change affects that crate's public API / usage example, its install or feature story, or its published status (a stub ascending to published, a renamed/added feature flag); if so, bring its `crates/<crate>/README.md` into line on the same branch — and also the facade `crates/paigasus-helikon/README.md` and the root `README.md` whenever the crate roster or the feature → module map changes. README install snippets deliberately use drift-free `cargo add` (no hardcoded versions), so a routine version bump alone needs no README edit. Like the mdBook, the READMEs drift silently otherwise — they sat as untouched 3-line SMA-304 stubs (`Stub — see SMA-304`) through all of Stage 1 while ten crates shipped real implementations; SMA-424 is the one-time catch-up, and this rule keeps the backlog from rebuilding. A pure-internal change (refactor, CI, deps, release plumbing) needs no README edit — but make that a conscious call, not a silent skip.
- Commit prefix: `<type>(<scope>): SMA-### <message>` (e.g. `feat(facade): SMA-304 ...`).
- **PR titles must satisfy two independent rules from `pr-title.yml`** (`amannn/action-semantic-pull-request`):
  1. **Full Conventional Commits format.** The action enforces a valid `type(scope):` prefix from the action's configured `types` list — independent of the subject regex. `SMA-317 add anthropic provider` (no prefix) fails; `feat(providers-anthropic): SMA-317 add anthropic provider` passes.
  2. **Subject must start lowercase after the `SMA-###` prefix.** The `subjectPattern: ^([A-Z]{2,4}-\d+ )?[^A-Z].+$` rejects `feat(core): SMA-314 LlmAgent + ...` because `L` is uppercase; lead the subject with a lowercase verb (`add`, `wire`, `pin`, `promote`, `implement`, `fix`).
  Per-commit Conventional Commit titles on the feature branch don't trip either rule — only the PR title (which becomes the squashed `main` commit) is gated.
- Linear auto-closes the linked SMA-* issue when its PR merges; no manual status move needed.
- **Always implement GitHub Actions against the latest stable major**, pinned to a commit SHA (never a moving `@vN` tag), keeping the human-readable version as a trailing `# vX.Y.Z` comment **on the `uses:` line**, so the SHA is auditable. The comment must end with the version: Dependabot updates only a same-line comment that ends with the old version, so a version on its own line above the step goes stale on every bump (SMA-744). This rule applies only to pins of a tagged release. `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` is pinned to an untagged `master` commit, so it has no version comment. Do not add one, because no tag gives a correct version. The `gh-actions` Dependabot group sets no `update-types`, so its configuration permits major bumps in the same grouped PR. Do not depend on that: `actions/checkout` still sat on v6.0.2 until SMA-486 bumped it by hand, so **check for a new major by hand**. `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` is a special case: it ships rolling branches and a periodically re-pointed `v1` tag, so confirm the direction (`ahead_by > 0, behind_by == 0`) before accepting any bump — the naive "bump to latest release" recipe once would have proposed an ~11-month downgrade. Independently and permanently: every site pinning it **must** pair the SHA with an explicit `with: toolchain: …`, because a SHA ref carries no toolchain selector. Recipes and history: `docs/runbooks/github-actions-pinning.md`.
- **After a PR merges to `main`, release-plz opens/updates a `chore: release` PR** (authored by the paigasusbot App) carrying the version bumps + CHANGELOG; in the normal flow **merging that PR is what publishes to crates.io** (the merged feature PR left versions matching the registry, so its own `main` push publishes nothing). The exception is a PR that bumps its own version — the stub-ascend ritual — which publishes on its own merge with no separate release PR. Check the release PR after every merge and watch its CI — its release-PR `cargo update` can pull a fresh advisory that reddens `audit`/`deny` on the bot PR **only** (independent of `main`); fix with a `chore(deps)` pin and release-plz regenerates the PR clean.

## CI

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs nine jobs on every PR (`commits` is PR-only; the other eight also run on push to `main`): `fmt`, `clippy`, `test` (matrix `{ubuntu, macos, windows} × {stable, 1.94}`, `fail-fast: false`), `build-no-default-features`, `docs` (`RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings`), `doc-coverage` (gated at `DOC_COVERAGE_THRESHOLD`, default 80%), `commits` (`convco check`), `sessions-it` (Postgres/Redis, path-filtered), and `markdown-lint`. The `paigasus-helikon-cli` crate is excluded from both the `missing_docs` lint and the coverage aggregator until its public API stabilizes.

`.github/workflows/integration.yml` runs `temporal-it` and `agentcore-image` as **signal-only** jobs, deliberately outside `ci.yml` so an expected flake cannot make "ci is red on `main`" meaningless. **Signal-only means *not listed as required*, never `continue-on-error`.**

`.github/workflows/msrv.yml` runs `cargo msrv --path crates/paigasus-helikon-core verify` as a non-required signal that the declared MSRV is truthful.

Supply-chain workflows (`audit.yml`, `deny.yml`, `sbom.yml`) are separate from `ci.yml` because they have independent triggers and failure semantics. `audit.yml` and `deny.yml` both run on push to `main`, PRs, a daily cron, and `workflow_dispatch`, so `main` is re-evaluated daily at exactly PR severity.

**To read an audit verdict, use the Checks API, not the legacy commit-status API** — the latter returns only `CodeRabbit` on this repo, rendering a confident `state: success` that contains no audit verdict whatsoever:

```bash
gh api repos/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/commits/main/check-runs \
  --jq '.check_runs[] | select(.name=="audit" or .name=="deny") | {name, status, conclusion}'
```

Note also that the `scheduled-audit` job's green status means nothing at any severity — read the *run* conclusion, never that job's status.

The required-status-check contexts gated on `main` are (bare job names, as posted by the GitHub Actions app): `fmt`, `clippy`, `test (ubuntu-latest, stable)`, `test (macos-latest, stable)`, `test (windows-latest, stable)`, `docs`, `doc-coverage`, `book-build`, `commits`, `pr-title`, `audit`, `deny`, `sessions-it`, `build-no-default-features`, `markdown-lint`. The macOS job is required because it is the only gate that compiles and runs the Seatbelt backend; the Windows job because it is the only gate that exercises the Windows timeout path in `paigasus-helikon-tools` — `cmd /C` process spawning and a `TerminateProcess`-based kill, which unlike the unix path has no process-group semantics and assigns a real exit code (SMA-569); `sessions-it` because it is the only gate that runs the live Postgres/Redis session backends; `build-no-default-features` because it is the only gate that compiles `runtime-axum` and `runtime-actix` with default features off. The canonical declaration is `.github/rulesets/main-protection-checks.json` (see CONTRIBUTING.md → "Repo configuration"). Other matrix variants (the `1.94` legs) run as signals only.

These pins are hand-bumped with nothing tracking them: `TEMPORAL_CLI_VERSION`/`TEMPORAL_CLI_SHA256` in `integration.yml`, `NIGHTLY_TOOLCHAIN` in `ci.yml`, `convco@…` in `ci.yml`'s `commits` job, `MDBOOK_VERSION`/`MDBOOK_LINKCHECK_VERSION` in `docs.yml`, and `markdownlint-cli2` via `package-lock.json`. **A checksum mismatch is never a signal to update the digest** — the causes are, in order, a truncated download, an upstream re-tag, and tampering; verify upstream independently first.

**The workspace needs no system `protoc`** (SMA-623): `temporalio-client`'s `vendored-protox` feature compiles the Temporal protos with `protox`. `ci.yml` sets `PROTOC` to a path that does not exist, and `build-no-default-features` asserts that the feature is active. If a build fails with "Could not find `protoc`", do not add a `protoc` install — find which build script calls it. Rationale and recovery: `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md` → "protoc and protox".

Job-by-job rationale, the audit/deny signal semantics, and the incident history behind all of the above: `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md`.

**GitHub's 10 GB Actions cache limit is a standing constraint, not a one-time cleanup** (SMA-618): it is GitHub's **default**, not a hard ceiling — a repo admin, org owner or enterprise owner can raise it (user-owned repos up to 10 TB) at additional storage cost, and SMA-618 deliberately chose to fit inside it rather than pay. Enforced at 10 **GiB** (10,737,418,240 bytes) despite the "10 GB" wording. Going over fails nothing — it just triggers silent LRU eviction that makes CI legs run cold at random. `cache-budget.yml` monitors it daily and warns (never fails) above 8.5 GiB. Caches are saved **only** from `main` (`save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}` on every `Swatinem/rust-cache` site) so a PR job can still restore an entry `main` wrote but never writes a competing `refs/pull/N/merge` entry that evicts it. The `CARGO_*`/`RUST*`-prefixed workflow env that `rust-cache` hashes into its key must stay byte-identical across every cache-bearing workflow, enforced by `scripts/check-cargo-profile-env-sync.sh` running as a step in `fmt`. `audit` and `deny` deliberately cache no `target/` directory — neither compiles the workspace, so it was pure waste against the fixed budget.  CI also sets **`CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG: line-tables-only`** (SMA-618 PR 2), which measured a **16.5% cut in total cache bytes** — 14-29% on the `test` legs and exactly 0% on `clippy`/`docs`/`doc-coverage`, which are metadata-mode builds with no debug info to remove. (A local sample of the largest `.rlib` files suggested 79%; do not extrapolate an aggregate from its densest component.) Keeping line tables preserves file:line in panic backtraces. Like `CARGO_TERM_COLOR`, it is **inside** rust-cache's key, so it must be byte-identical in every cache-bearing workflow — adding it to one and not the rest silently splits the cache rather than failing. `prefix-key: v1` marks the post-PR-2 generation, so any surviving `v0-` entry is provably stale and safe to purge — note it **replaces** the default `v0-rust` entirely, so keys read `v1-<job>-...`, not `v1-rust-<job>-...`. `clippy` and `docs` share one entry via `shared-key: metadata`, with `clippy` the sole writer and `docs` carrying a literal `save-if: false`; exactly one site may save a shared key, and the guard enforces it. Full rationale: `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md` → "Actions cache budget".

The **`microvm`/forkd live-KVM path is not validated locally or in GitHub CI** — the dev host is arm64 macOS (no `/dev/kvm`) and GitHub runners have none. Validate it on a **GCP nested-virtualization VM** (Ubuntu 24.04 — the forkd binaries need glibc ≥ 2.38; Intel `n2`) per `docs/runbooks/forkd-live-validation.md`. The `tests/forkd_live.rs` tests are env-gated (`FORKD_URL` / `FORKD_TOKEN` / `FORKD_SNAPSHOT`) and loud-skip when no controller is configured, so `cargo test` stays green without one.

## Local hooks

Hooks are managed via `cargo-husky` (user-hooks mode) and live in `.cargo-husky/hooks/`. They install into `.git/hooks/` on the next dev-dep realization of `paigasus-helikon`. To force a re-install after editing one: `rm -rf target/debug/build/cargo-husky-* && cargo test -p paigasus-helikon --no-run`.

- **`commit-msg`** — runs `convco check --from-stdin` (enforces the `.versionrc` allowlist).
- **`pre-commit`** — intentional no-op (`exit 0`). The file exists to claim the slot so future cargo-husky upgrades don't fill it in with surprise behavior.
- **`pre-push`** — runs `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `convco check <merge-base>..HEAD`. Catches the three fastest CI gates pre-push; deliberately omits `cargo test` and `cargo doc` (too slow for every push). Bypass for WIP branches: `git push --no-verify`.

Three rules here are easy to get wrong, and each has already cost a debugging session:

- **The re-install silently does nothing inside a git worktree** — cargo-husky searches for a `.git` *directory* and a worktree's is a file, so it installs nothing and the old hook keeps running. Run the re-install from the **main checkout**, and verify with `grep` against the installed copy rather than assuming.
- **Never hand-copy a hook onto `.git/hooks/<name>`** — on this machine the Entire CLI owns `pre-push` and chains to `.git/hooks/pre-push.pre-entire`, which is where the cargo-husky hook actually lives. Check for a `.pre-entire` sibling first and install into that slot.
- **The convco baseline must be a merge-base, not a branch tip** — `convco check A..B` silently falls back to walking the entire history when `A` is not an ancestor of `B`, rejecting correct branches with failures the author did not write.

Mechanics and the SMA-547 postmortem: `docs/runbooks/local-hooks.md`.

`.gitattributes` pins `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/tests/fixtures/*.txt` to `text eol=lf`. The streaming tests `include_str!` the SSE fixtures and split them on literal `\n` delimiters; without this, Windows checkouts produce CRLF bytes and the literal-string splits return one part instead of two. When adding wire-format fixtures elsewhere that the test code parses byte-level, extend the rule.

34:- Run A: `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `thinking: {"type":"adaptive"}`, `output_config.effort: "high"`,
35:  beta `interleaved-thinking-2025-05-14`.
36:- Run B: `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `thinking: {"type":"enabled","budget_tokens":2048}`, same beta.
37:- Run C: `claude-sonnet-4-5` and `claude-opus-4-5`, `enabled` with budget 2048, **no beta header**
38:  (the SDK default).
39:
40:Wire format:
41:
42:- A `thinking` block starts with `content_block_start`
43:  `{"type":"thinking","thinking":"","signature":""}`. Then `thinking_delta` events, then exactly one
44:  `signature_delta`, then `content_block_stop`.
45:- On `claude-sonnet-5-5` the thinking text is empty and only the signature arrives (988 to 1180
46:  characters). On the 4.5 models the text arrives (106 to 256 characters) with a signature (528 to
47:  732 characters).
48:- A `redacted_thinking` block arrives whole in `content_block_start`:
49:  `{"type":"redacted_thinking","data":"…"}`, with no delta, then `content_block_stop`. Runs B and C
50:  produced 14 or 15 of them in one response (384 to 440 characters each), with the documented test
51:  trigger string in the prompt.
52:- A `tool_use` block start now also has a `caller` key. The SDK ignores it.
53:- The observed order was always thinking (or redacted) blocks, then `text`, then `tool_use`. No
54:  response had interleaved thinking inside one response.
55:- `claude-sonnet-5-5` rejects `{"type":"enabled"}` with HTTP 400 ("\"thinking.type.enabled\" is not
56:  supported for this model. Use \"thinking.type.adaptive\" and \"output_config.effort\""). With
80:   Anthropic parts and must build as on `main`; the new turns must be ordered (Task 3 test
81:   `mixed_old_and_new_turns`).
82:3. **A response with ten or more blocks** (run C produced 15 redacted blocks). Index 10 must sort
83:   after index 2, not before it (Task 3 test `two_digit_indexes_sort_numerically`).
84:4. **Two `text` blocks in one response** (`thinking, text A, tool_use, thinking, text B, tool_use`).
165:  The `#[allow(dead_code)]` on `SignatureDelta::signature` and on `ContentBlockStop::index` goes.

168:  parser ignores. Replace every signature with `SIG_FAKE_<n>` and every redacted `data` with
169:  `REDACTED_FAKE_<n>`. Remove trailing spaces inside `data:` lines. Keep every other byte of a
170:  transcribed event.
171:  - `thinking_text_tool_use.txt`: from `probe-840-c-claude-sonnet-4-5/1-turn1.sse` (all events).

174:    `message_start`, the redacted blocks with index 0 and 1, the `text` block and the `tool_use`
175:    block, `message_delta`, `message_stop`. Remove the redacted blocks with index 2 to 13. Change
176:    the text index 14 to 2 and the `tool_use` index 15 to 3. Say this in the comment line.
177:  - `empty_thinking_tool_use.txt`: from `probe-840-a/1-turn1.sse` (claude-sonnet-5-5, the thinking
178:    text is empty, one `thinking_delta` with `""`).
179:  - `interleaved_thinking.txt` (synthetic; comment `: synthetic, no capture has interleaved
180:    thinking`): the run C envelope, then thinking index 0 (`"Need the code."`, `SIG_FAKE_1`),
181:    `tool_use` index 1 id `toolu_fake_b` name `lookup_city_code` input `{"city":"Paris"}`,
182:    thinking index 2 (`"Now the weather."`, `SIG_FAKE_2`), `tool_use` index 3 id `toolu_fake_a`
183:    name `weather_by_code` input `{"code":"PAR-7351"}`, stop reason `tool_use`. The ids sort in
184:    the other order than the stream order on purpose.
185:  - `unsigned_thinking_tool_use.txt` (synthetic): a thinking block with two `thinking_delta`
186:    events and no `signature_delta`, then one `tool_use` block, stop reason `tool_use`.
187:- [ ] **Step 2: Check the fixtures.** Run

    "So the captures are not the source of this file.",
]

    "comparison, not a source. The comparison set is two files in this "
    "directory from SMA-840 (PR #387): empty_thinking_tool_use.txt (run A, "
    "claude-sonnet-5-5) and thinking_text_tool_use.txt (run C, "
    "claude-sonnet-4-5). The two files have the same keys for each event "
    "type. The comparison inherits the edit lists in their headers. Nobody "
    "has checked those lists against a raw capture. For each event type in "
    "this file, every key is compared in both directions.",
    "",
]

MSG_START = (
    "- message_start: the captures also carry message.container, "
    "message.stop_sequence, message.stop_details, message.diagnostics, "
    "usage.cache_creation (with ephemeral_5m_input_tokens and "
    "ephemeral_1h_input_tokens), usage.service_tier, usage.inference_geo and "
    "usage.speed. This file has no key that the captures do not have. The "
    "captures put model first in message. This file puts it after content. "
    "The captures put cache_creation_input_tokens before "
    "cache_read_input_tokens. This file has the opposite order. The captures "
    "send output_tokens 7 (run A) and 3 (run C). This file sends 0."
)
MSG_DELTA = (
    "- message_delta: the captures also carry delta.stop_details, "
    "delta.container, usage.input_tokens, usage.cache_creation_input_tokens, "
    "usage.cache_read_input_tokens and usage.output_tokens_details "
    "(thinking_tokens). This file carries only usage.output_tokens."
)
PING = (
    "- ping: each capture sends a ping event after its first "
    "content_block_start. This file has no ping event."
)
TOOL_START = (
    "- content_block_start (tool_use): the captures also carry "
    "\"caller\":{\"type\":\"direct\"}. The other keys and their order are the "

TOOL_INPUT = (
    "- input_json_delta: the keys are the same. The captures send a first "

    "the whole input in one delta for each block."

    "thinking block."

END_TURN = (
    "- No capture: stop_reason \"end_turn\". Both captures stop with "
    "\"tool_use\"."
)
ERROR = (
    "- No capture: the error event. No comparison file has one."
)

    END_TURN,

    "",

]

HEADERS["parallel_tool_use.txt"] = SOURCE_317 + CMP_INTRO + [

def wrap(par):
    if par == "":
        return [":"]
    sub = "  " if par.startswith("- ") else ""
    lines = textwrap.wrap(
        par,
        width=WIDTH - 2,
        subsequent_indent=sub,
        break_long_words=False,
        break_on_hyphens=False,
    )
    return [": " + line for line in lines]


def strip_header(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    lines = data.split(b"\n")
    i = 0
    while i < len(lines) - 1 and (lines[i].startswith(b":") or lines[i] == b""):
        i += 1
    return b"\n".join(lines[i:])


for name, pars in HEADERS.items():
    path = os.path.join(D, name)
    with open(path, "rb") as fh:
        old = fh.read()
    body = strip_header(old)
    out = []
    for par in pars:
        out += wrap(par)
    header = ("\n".join(out) + "\n\n").encode("utf-8")
    with open(path, "wb") as fh:
        fh.write(header + body)
    print(name, len(out), "header lines")

def wrap(par):
    if par == "":
        return [":"]
    sub = "  " if par.startswith("- ") else ""
    lines = textwrap.wrap(
        par,
        width=WIDTH - 2,
        subsequent_indent=sub,
        break_long_words=False,
        break_on_hyphens=False,
    )
    return [": " + line for line in lines]


def strip_header(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    lines = data.split(b"\n")
    i = 0
    while i < len(lines) - 1 and (lines[i].startswith(b":") or lines[i] == b""):
        i += 1
    return b"\n".join(lines[i:])


for name, pars in HEADERS.items():
    path = os.path.join(D, name)
    with open(path, "rb") as fh:
        old = fh.read()
    body = strip_header(old)
    out = []
    for par in pars:
        out += wrap(par)
    header = ("\n".join(out) + "\n\n").encode("utf-8")
    with open(path, "wb") as fh:
        fh.write(header + body)
    print(name, len(out), "header lines")

# Task 10 report: Anthropic and SMA-840 fixture headers

Status: DONE_WITH_CONCERNS

Commit: `e02dc286 test(providers): SMA-845 state the provenance of the anthropic fixtures`
(signed, `%G?` = G).

## What changed

- `tests/workspace-lints/tests/fixture_provenance_header.rs`: `ALLOWLIST` is now `&[]`. The doc
  line now says "Phase B of SMA-845 emptied it."
- 14 fixtures in `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/tests/fixtures/` have a D1 header:
  - HAND-AUTHORED (SMA-317, PR #33): `text_only`, `parallel_tool_use`, `thinking_then_text`,
    `tool_use_then_continuation`, `stream_error`.
  - HAND-AUTHORED (SMA-531, PR #200): `eof_after_message_delta`, `body_cut_inside_message_stop`,
    `eof_mid_content_block`, `error_after_message_delta`.
  - CAPTURED (SMA-840, PR #387), with Removed, Added and Changed: `thinking_text_tool_use`,
    `empty_thinking_tool_use`, `redacted_thinking_tool_use`.
  - HAND-AUTHORED (SMA-840, PR #387), each names the capture it copies: `interleaved_thinking`,
    `unsigned_thinking_tool_use`.
- The headers were made by a script (scratchpad `headers.py`) that strips the leading `:`/blank
  block and writes a new one. Lines wrap at 78 columns. Seven lines are 84 to 86 columns, because
  each holds one unbroken SMA-840 design path.

## Verification

- Step 1: with the allowlist empty and no headers, the walker test failed on exactly 14 files
  (`MissingProvenanceLine` for each).
- Byte-exact data check (python3 -I, byte mode): for all 14 files, the content after the leading
  `:`/blank block equals `git show 6c2153df:<path>` with its leading block stripped. Result:
  ALL OK.
- `body_cut_inside_message_stop.txt` last byte is `0x61` (not `0x0a`).
- `# --- turn 2 ---` is still a data-area line (1 occurrence), outside the header.
- `git check-attr eol` on the fixtures: `eol: lf`.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p paigasus-helikon-workspace-lints --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test -p paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic`: pass (239 unit, plus integration
  suites; 6 + 10 + 1 ignored live tests).
- `cargo test -p paigasus-helikon-workspace-lints`: pass (incl. both walker tests).
- `cargo test -p paigasus-helikon-provider-stream-conformance`: pass (46 + 12).
- The cited SMA-840 paths exist on `origin/main` (52a74cca, PR #387): the probe script and the
  five SMA-840 fixtures. HEAD contains `origin/main`.

## Key diff per D3

Method: a script parsed each `data:` line, grouped events by type (`content_block_start` by block
type, `content_block_delta` by delta type), and diffed every nested key path in both directions
against the comparison set. It also compared key order on the shared keys at each level.
Comparison set: `empty_thinking_tool_use.txt` (run A) and `thinking_text_tool_use.txt` (run C).
`redacted_thinking_tool_use.txt` is excluded (D3). The two comparison files have identical key
structure for every event type (checked).

Result, the same for every SMA-317/SMA-531 fixture where the event type occurs:

| Event type | Only in captures | Only in fixture | Key order |
|---|---|---|---|
| `message_start` | `message.container`, `message.stop_sequence`, `message.stop_details`, `message.diagnostics`, `usage.cache_creation{ephemeral_5m_input_tokens, ephemeral_1h_input_tokens}`, `usage.service_tier`, `usage.inference_geo`, `usage.speed` | none | captures: `model` first in `message`; fixtures: `id,type,role,content,model,...`. captures: `cache_creation_input_tokens` before `cache_read_input_tokens`; fixtures: opposite |
| `content_block_start` (text) | none | none | same |
| `content_block_start` (thinking) | `content_block.signature` | none | same |
| `content_block_start` (tool_use) | `content_block.caller{type}` | none | same |
| `text_delta`, `thinking_delta`, `signature_delta`, `input_json_delta` | none | none | same |
| `content_block_stop`, `message_stop` | none | none | same |
| `message_delta` | `delta.stop_details`, `delta.container`, `usage.input_tokens`, `usage.cache_creation_input_tokens`, `usage.cache_read_input_tokens`, `usage.output_tokens_details{thinking_tokens}` | none | same on shared keys |
| `ping` | present in captures (after first `content_block_start`) | absent from all nine | n/a |
| `error` | no capture | in `stream_error`, `error_after_message_delta` | n/a |

Value-level points recorded in headers: captures send `message_start` `output_tokens` 7 (run A)
and 3 (run C), fixtures send 0. Captures send a first `"partial_json":""` delta, then three
fragments; fixtures send one whole delta. Placeholders: `msg_01`..`msg_06`, `msg_04a/b`, `tu_a`,
`tu_b`, `tu_weather`, model `claude-sonnet-4-6`, signature `abc123`.

Shapes with no capture (written as "No capture"): `stop_reason "end_turn"`, a turn without
thinking, two `tool_use` blocks in sequence, a turn with no text block (`parallel_tool_use`),
thinking then text with no `tool_use` (`thinking_then_text`), a second response body after a
tool result (`tool_use_then_continuation`), the `error` event, a body that ends after `error`.

Byte facts checked for the SMA-531 files: `eof_after_message_delta`, `body_cut_inside_message_stop`
and `eof_mid_content_block` are byte prefixes of `text_only.txt` (lengths 849, 889, 518 of 900).
The `error` data line in `error_after_message_delta.txt` is byte-identical to the one in
`stream_error.txt`. For the synthetic SMA-840 files: the `message_start`, `message_delta` and
`message_stop` data lines are byte-identical to `thinking_text_tool_use.txt`; neither has `ping`.

P531 = `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-16-sma-531-anthropic-eof-finish-flush.md`;
S840 = `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-21-sma-840-anthropic-thinking-signatures-design.md`;

# Task 10 review: Anthropic and SMA-840 fixture headers

Range: 6c2153df..e02dc286 (one commit, `e02dc286`). Reviewer: read-only. All paths are relative to
the worktree root. Fixture paths are under
`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/tests/fixtures/`.

### Spec Compliance

- ✅ Spec compliant. All 14 fixtures carry a D1 header. The labels match the evidence. `ALLOWLIST`
  is `&[]` (`tests/workspace-lints/tests/fixture_provenance_header.rs:11`). The three CAPTURED files
  have Removed, Added and Changed. The two synthetic SMA-840 files are HAND-AUTHORED and name the
  capture whose envelope they copy. `# --- turn 2 ---` stays in the data area
  (`tool_use_then_continuation.txt:84`).
- ⚠️ Cannot verify from the diff: nothing. I checked the data bytes, the key diff and the cited
  lines directly (see below).

### Claims checked

Data invariance and byte facts (own python3 -I script, read-only):

- For all 14 files, the bytes after the leading `:`/blank block equal those at `6c2153df` →
  confirmed. Only the leading block changed.
- `body_cut_inside_message_stop.txt` last byte `0x61`, last line `data: {"type":"messa` → confirmed.
- `eof_after_message_delta` (849 B), `body_cut_inside_message_stop` (889 B), `eof_mid_content_block`
  (518 B, three events) are byte prefixes of `text_only.txt` (900 B) → confirmed.
- `error_after_message_delta.txt`: every data line except `msg_06` `message_start` and the `error`
  line is a line of `text_only.txt`; its `error` line equals `stream_error.txt:51` → confirmed.
- Synthetic SMA-840 files: `message_start`, `message_delta`, `message_stop` equal run C's → confirmed
  (diff context lines 289 / 762 against 584). Neither has `ping` → confirmed.

Key diff (own script, both directions, per event type):

- Run A and run C files have the same key paths for every event type → confirmed.
- Every "captures also carry" list for `message_start`, `message_delta`, thinking start
  (`signature`), tool_use start (`caller` = `{"type":"direct"}`) → confirmed. "This file has no key
  that the captures do not have" → confirmed for all nine.
- Key order (`model` first; `cache_creation_input_tokens` before `cache_read_input_tokens`) →
  confirmed from the data lines.
- `output_tokens` 7 (run A) / 3 (run C) / 0 (fixtures) → confirmed.
- Captures: first `"partial_json":""`, then three fragments; fixtures: one whole delta → confirmed.
- `ping` after the first `content_block_start` in A and C → confirmed. Ping is the only data line
  with a space after a key colon (other `": ` hits are inside `partial_json` string values) →
  confirmed.
- "No capture" items (end_turn, no thinking, two tool_use, no text block, thinking-then-text without
  tool_use, second body, error, body ending after error) → confirmed against the event lists of A
  and C.

Cited sources:

- SMA-317 design line 465 quote → confirmed verbatim.
- PR #33 merged 2026-05-26 (`gh pr view 33`: 2026-05-26T21:29:15Z) → confirmed. PR #200 (SMA-531)
  and PR #387 (SMA-840) are the right PRs → confirmed.
- SMA-531 plan 180, 211, 572-573, 587-593 → confirmed. 573 names no source → confirmed.
- SMA-840 design 27 (date), 29-32 (raw captures not in repo, real signatures), 34-35 (run A),
  37-38 (run C), 42-44 (one `signature_delta`), 45-47 (lengths), 48-51 (redacted, trigger),
  53-54 and 102-103 (no interleaving), 369 (addendum) → confirmed.
- SMA-840 plan 167-170 (comment line, SIG_FAKE / REDACTED_FAKE, trailing spaces, keep bytes), 171,
  173-176, 177-178, 179-184, 185-186, 82 (15 redacted blocks) → confirmed.
- Probe script 33-34 (tool names), 42 (endpoint), 77 (PAR-7351) → confirmed.
- Test delimiter split at `tests/messages_streaming.rs:202` and `src/stream.rs:1122` → confirmed.
- SMA-845 spec D3 "which nobody has checked" (line 199-200) → supports "Nobody has checked those
  lists against a raw capture".
- "The record does not name the prompt of run A, turn 1" → **not confirmed** (I1).

### Strengths

- The key diff is exact. I reproduced every list and every "no key only in the fixture" claim.
- Inferences are labelled as inferences (14 redacted blocks; usage counts include removed blocks).
- The 15-vs-14 tension is surfaced, not hidden.
- The headers say "the plan says" for SMA-840 instructions, not "was done". This is the correct
  reading of the record.
- The two controller rulings hold. The scratchpad captures are temporary, and the SMA-840 plan
  line 42 forbids copying capture values, so a header must not cite them. A line of 84-86 columns
  that holds one unbroken path cannot wrap without breaking the path; this is acceptable.

### Issues

#### Critical (Must Fix)

None. I found no invented value.

#### Important (Should Fix)

**I1. `empty_thinking_tool_use.txt:14-18` omits the evidence that exists for the run A turn-1
prompt.**

- Claim: the addendum says the earlier probes got thinking because the prompt started with the
  trigger string. Then: "The record does not name the prompt of run A, turn 1."
- What the source says: the probe script that the same header cites (line 20-24 of the header)
  names the turn-1 prompt. `1-turn1` is sent with `$PROMPT` (probe line 100, 103). `$PROMPT`
  defaults to `BASE_PROMPT` with no trigger string (lines 36-37). The trigger is added only for
  `16-redacted` (line 170). This conflicts with the addendum's reading, and the reader sees only the
  addendum. The constraints say: if the record is silent, write "not recorded" **and the evidence
  that does exist**. The record is not silent here; it is partial and contrary.
- Suggested wording (replace the last sentence at line 17-18):

  ```text
  : The record does not say which prompt run A, turn 1 used. In the merged
  : probe script, turn 1 sends $PROMPT (line 100). $PROMPT defaults to a
  : prompt with no trigger string (lines 36-37). Only the 16-redacted request
  : adds the trigger string (line 170). The run can have set PROMPT, or used an
  : earlier script version.
  ```

#### Minor (Nice to Have)

**M1. `redacted_thinking_tool_use.txt:25-28` leaves out design line 50.** The header sets plan
line 82 ("15") against the inferred 14 and says the record does not resolve it. SMA-840 design
line 50 says "Runs B and C produced 14 or 15 of them in one response". This fits a count of 14 in
`16-redacted.sse`. Suggested addition after "...which run C response that count is from.":
`: The design says that runs B and C produced 14 or 15 redacted blocks in one
: response (line 50).`

**M2. `interleaved_thinking.txt:24-26` and `unsigned_thinking_tool_use.txt:23-25` describe only the
`city` input.** `interleaved_thinking.txt` has a second tool block with fragments `""`,
`{"code":`, `"PAR-7351"}`. Suggested wording for `interleaved_thinking.txt`:
`: - Tool input fragments: "", then {"city": and "Paris"} for index 1, and "",
:   then {"code": and "PAR-7351"} for index 3. The captures split the city
:   input at other places. The captures have no weather_by_code call. The
:   record does not give a source for these splits.`

**M3. `interleaved_thinking.txt:20-23` cites only the probe script for the tool names and
PAR-7351.** The direct source is the SMA-840 plan, lines 181-183, which give the ids, names and
inputs. The probe-script citation is correct but secondary. Suggested: "The tool names and inputs
come from the plan (lines 181-183). The names match the probe script (lines 33-34)."

**M4. `body_cut_inside_message_stop.txt:13` "The cut does not change a shape."** The cut does
change the final `message_stop` event, as line 8-9 of the same header says. Suggested: "The cut
does not change the shape of any whole event."

**M5. `unsigned_thinking_tool_use.txt:5` "So no capture has this shape."** This is an inference
from the design's wire-format summary (lines 42-44), stated as fact. Suggested: "So the SMA-840
record shows no capture with this shape. The design calls the file synthetic (line 275)."

**M6. All three CAPTURED headers (for example `empty_thinking_tool_use.txt:20-24`): the merged
probe defaults differ from the recorded run settings.** The merged script defaults to
`claude-sonnet-5-5`, adaptive thinking with `block_binding`, and the beta
`thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01` (probe lines 19-24). Run A used
`interleaved-thinking-2025-05-14`; run C used no beta. The headers already say the run version is
not recorded. One sentence would show why that matters: "The merged script's defaults (lines
19-24) are not the run A or run C settings. So the run set environment overrides, or used an
earlier version."

### Assessment

**Task quality:** Approved with fixes (fix I1; M1-M6 are optional).

**Reasoning:** Every value, citation, byte fact and key-diff claim that I checked is correct, and no
data byte changed. One "not recorded" statement leaves out contrary evidence in a file the header
itself cites.

: "${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY:?set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}"
if [ "${ENABLED_PATH:-0}" = 1 ]; then
  MODEL="${MODEL:-claude-haiku-4-5}"
  DEFAULT_THINKING='{"type":"enabled","budget_tokens":2048}'
  DEFAULT_BETA="interleaved-thinking-2025-05-14"
else
  MODEL="${MODEL:-claude-sonnet-5-5}"
  DEFAULT_THINKING='{"type":"adaptive","block_binding":{"prefix_mismatch_behavior":"drop_block"}}'
  DEFAULT_BETA="thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01"
fi
THINKING="${THINKING:-$DEFAULT_THINKING}"
BETA="${BETA-$DEFAULT_BETA}"
BASE_PROMPT="What is the weather in Paris? First look up the city code, then get the weather with that code. Think briefly before each step."
PROMPT="${PROMPT:-$BASE_PROMPT}"
---
    "$(jq -r '[.content[]?.type] | join(",")' "$OUT/$1.resp.json")" \
    "in=$(jq -r '.usage.input_tokens // "-"' "$OUT/$1.resp.json") $(jq -r '.error.message // ""' "$OUT/$1.resp.json" | cut -c1-160)"
}

echo "== model: $MODEL  thinking: $THINKING  beta: ${BETA:-none}  extra: $EXTRA"
U1="$(jq -n --arg p "$PROMPT" '[{role:"user", content:$p}]')"

# 1. Turn 1, streamed.
stream_turn 1-turn1 "$U1" "$THINKING" "$MODEL"
B1="$(blocks_from_sse "$OUT/1-turn1.sse")"; echo "$B1" > "$OUT/1-blocks.json"
summarize_blocks "$B1"
R1="$(result_for "$B1")"
---
else
  echo "turn 2 made no tool call; third turns skipped"
fi

# 16. Redacted thinking, streamed, then the round trip.
UR="$(jq -n --arg p "$REDACT_TRIGGER $BASE_PROMPT" '[{role:"user", content:$p}]')"
stream_turn 16-redacted "$UR" "$THINKING" "$MODEL"
BR="$(blocks_from_sse "$OUT/16-redacted.sse")"; echo "$BR" > "$OUT/16-blocks.json"

  - `interleaved_thinking.txt` (synthetic, marked as such in a comment): thinking, `tool_use`,
    thinking, `tool_use`;
  - `unsigned_thinking_tool_use.txt` (synthetic): a thinking block with no `signature_delta`, then
    `tool_use`.
